A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TokenUnify, with matching authors, the same core research framework, and many retained results. Both complete 28-page documents, including their appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original EM neuron-segmentation experiments, scaling analyses, ablations, and appendix experiments reconstructing Kodak images.

after.justification: v2 retains original segmentation, scaling, and Kodak reconstruction results and adds evaluated baselines and a next-token-only ablation.

M1.justification: v1 Section 3.2 alternates prediction tasks every 100 epochs. v2 Section 4.2.4 specifies a weighted joint objective with curriculum transitions at 30% and 70% of training; Section 9.2 additionally introduces stochastic mode switching and Algorithm 4. These substantially change the reported optimization procedure, although the schedules are not reconciled. v1's adaptive Mamba-ordering formulation is also absent. The anisotropic EMmamba decoder was already documented in v1.

E1.justification: The EM pretraining datasets, MEC/AC3/4 segmentation, and LAION-5B-to-Kodak reconstruction coverage remain. However, v1 Section 5 and Figure 4 report Transformer scaling on CREMI, whereas v2 Figure 6 reports MEC only. The introductory change from 120 million to 1.2 billion annotated voxels does not establish dataset expansion: v1 Section 4 already reports 1.2 billion voxels across the same six volumes.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add evaluated BYOL, dbMIM, and MS-Con-EM comparisons on EMmamba while removing MAE-pretrained Superhuman, MALA, PEA, and UNETR comparisons; their supervised versions remain. Corresponding membership changes occur in the uncertainty table. The autoregressive comparator in v1's Transformer scaling plot is removed from v2 Figure 6, although the Kodak autoregressive comparison remains.

E3.justification: v2 assigns the last 20 AC4 images to validation rather than testing and omits v1 Appendix D.1's conflicting AC3 label-fraction and semi-supervised protocol. Reported MEC voxel resolution changes from 8×8×40 nm in v1's main text, or 8×8×35 nm in its appendix, to 4×4×35 nm in v2 Section 8.2.1. These are revisions to reported settings, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Core training budgets, model sizes, and metrics remain.

E4.justification: v2 Table 3 adds a next-token-only ablation, reporting VOI 4.0418 and ARAND 0.4416, to test standalone autoregressive pretraining. The other objective-combination rows and the component-finetuning ablation match v1 Tables 6–7. Their relocation into the main text and the expanded discussion of existing Kodak results do not constitute additional experiments.

E5.justification: v1 Table 8 reports unspecified ± error bars. v2 Table 7 and Section 10.1 explicitly identify these as standard deviations across multiple runs. Neither version specifies the run count or seeds, so this clarifies uncertainty reporting without establishing that additional runs were performed.

E6.justification: Added baseline results and removed pretrained-backbone rows substantially revise the main comparisons. In Table 1, reported Wafer4/Waterz MAE VOI changes from 1.2680 to 1.3248 while TokenUnify remains 0.9951; the larger reported margin therefore does not reflect an improved TokenUnify score. The uncertainty table also corrects supervised PEA's Waterz mean VOI from 2.1531 to 1.3979. The next-token-only result is new, whereas all Kodak table values are retained.

T1.justification: v2 replaces v1's dimension-independent MAE bound with an ℓ1-regularized absolute-error estimator bound involving sqrt(s log p/n), revises its assumptions to restricted isometry, and reformulates the autoregressive theorem using a stationary AR(∞) process. It replaces the earlier next-all prediction error analysis with an ensemble-based derivation and adds information-complementarity, latent-manifold curvature, and alternating-optimization convergence theorems in Section 11.

C1.justification: v2 presents TokenUnify as a hierarchical predictive coding framework focused on neuron segmentation and adds central claims of optimal information coverage and O(K)-to-O(sqrt(K)) error reduction. These go beyond v1's general mixed-token prediction and scalability claims. The dataset novelty claim changes from the largest to one of the largest, and the headline advantage over MAE changes from 21% to 25%.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations involving local/sequential/global information, manifold geometry, and variance-based stability. It removes v1 Appendix E.1's explicit qualification that benefits may depend on 3D sequences and that natural-image downstream performance remains unvalidated. Section 10.2 instead interprets unchanged Kodak reconstruction results as evidence of broad cross-domain generalization, although future work still mentions other downstream tasks.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies 4×16×16 tokenization patches, a 2 TB MEC collection, two experts' six-month annotation effort, and annotation quality controls. Dataset metadata are revised. Conversely, v1's registration/denoising/interpolation description and explicit Waterz threshold of 0.5 and 256-bin discretization are omitted. Hardware, optimizer settings, architecture specifications, and the code URL are largely retained.

R1.justification: Related work shifts substantially from LLMs and multimodal learning toward neuron segmentation and affinity-based methods. v2 adds discussion and citations for MALIS, graph-based biological segmentation, cross-dimension affinity distillation, and other connectomics research, while removing much of the BERT/Qwen/CLIP/BLIP discussion. BYOL is newly cited; the works identified as dbMIM and MS-Con-EM were already cited in v1 but become evaluated comparators.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and method narrative are extensively rewritten around neuron segmentation and hierarchical prediction. v2 introduces a Theoretical Motivations section and a contents list, places dataset and implementation material before supplementary theory, and moves implementation details and social-impact discussion out of the main text.

P2.justification: v2 changes to a two-column layout, reorganizes comparison tables into supervised and self-supervised groups, and moves ablation tables into the main text. It adds MEC annotation illustrations, 3D segmentation comparisons, and Algorithm 4; expands the wafer-layer illustration; and redraws the scaling plot without the autoregressive curve. Existing prediction diagrams, the segmentation pipeline, and Kodak panels are retained.

improvement.justification: The added shared-backbone comparisons, next-token-only ablation, clarified standard deviations, and annotation documentation improve empirical assessability. However, v2 does not reconcile its weighted curriculum with its stochastic training protocol, and the specified softmax logits do not produce the stated weights. It also broadens generalization claims from unchanged Kodak evidence while removing explicit limitations. These gains coexist with material problems in reproducibility and claim calibration, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
